pages.text: At evening, the herd went down to the waterhole. Moya sniffed the water's scent. "Me first!" They raced ahead along the red dirt path. The adults were still on the hill, heads high, checking the shore.
Moya thrust their muzzle toward the water before the adults came down. Nia called from the hill, alarmed. "Moya, wait!"
Splash! Moya's front hoof sank into mud. "Oh?" The shore was slippery and deeper than expected. Moya struggled, then looked back at the grown-ups, cheeks hot with embarrassment.
Mom came down and supported Moya's neck with her muzzle, pulling them free. "My, you were thirsty!" Instead of scolding, she nuzzled Moya's nose and stood beside them.
Mom said gently, "A grown-up checks the shore first—slippery places, deep places. Grown-ups drink first, then children." She looked this way and that. Moya followed her gaze.
Nia explained, "One, the grown-ups check. Two, they take the first sip. Three, then we drink together!" Moya nodded and waited with all four hooves neatly together.
At last, Mom took a sip. "Let's all drink!" The herd lowered their heads side by side. This time, Moya waited before joining them. Grown-ups first!
Strangely, drinking together made the water cooler and sweeter! Moya stretched their neck beside Mom. "It tastes better together!" Nia lowered their long neck and drank, too.
Moya knew the waterhole rules. "One, grown-ups check! Two, grown-ups sip! Three, everyone together!" Next morning, Moya waited for the adults on the hill again.
After the drink, Mom curled her neck around Moya in a hug. "So grown-up!" Waiting until the adults had checked made drinking safer. Let the grown-ups drink first!
